- When sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is 1.00 or near 1.00, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with bullish sentiment.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce noise in 30d forecasts.
- If recent 3–5 day price range is narrow, model tends to predict mean reversion; adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is 0.20 or above, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days of forecast); apply 1–2% upward adjustment for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
